chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension in the setting of chronic HIV infection and multiple metabolic risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58-year-old white male with a longstanding diagnosis of HIV infection since 2003, currently on a three‑drug antiretroviral regimen (lamivudine/tenofovir, darunavir, ritonavir). Over the past two decades he has developed obesity (BMI >30), prediabetes (A1c 5.9%), stage 2 hypertension (BP 159/112 mmHg), obstructive sleep apnea, and anemia. He reports ongoing psychosocial stress, exposure to violence, and works part‑time, suggesting limited socioeconomic resources. He has had minimal outpatient engagement, with the last recorded encounter in January 2019, and no documented therapy for hypertension, dyslipidaemia, glucose control, sleep apnea, or anemia. This combination places him at high risk for cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications.
past_medical_history: History of appendectomy (1984). Resolved lacerations of hand and other injuries (2018). Prior full‑time employment and social isolation resolved in 2018. Medication review due items resolved in 2017–2018.

active_medications.name: lamivudine 300 MG / tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 MG Oral Tablet
darunavir 800 MG Oral Tablet
active_medications.purpose: Protease inhibitor component of HIV regimen

social_determinants: Part‑time employment suggesting limited income/insurance; reports of environmental violence and chronic stress; educated to high school level only; low documented social support; no smoking or alcohol data available.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk is markedly elevated: stage 2 hypertension (SBP 159/DBP 112), obesity, prediabetes, HIV‑associated inflammation, and probable dyslipidaemia (no lipid labs). Renal risk is uncertain due to missing eGFR and tenofovir exposure. Metabolic risk includes OSA and anemia. Charlson comorbidity index is 1 (HIV). Polypharmacy risk is low (3 meds). No data on smoking, cholesterol, LDL, or renal function limit full risk stratification.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing despite documented obesity
Renal function (eGFR) not recorded; important given tenofovir use and hypertension
Lipid panel missing; needed for ASCVD risk assessment
No antihypertensive agents listed despite stage 2 hypertension
No CPAP or other sleep‑apnea therapy documented
No iron, B12, folate, or erythropoiesis‑stimulating agents recorded
No TMP‑SMX or similar prophylaxis documented for HIV

clinical_impression: The patient presents with high‑risk cardiovascular and metabolic profile driven by uncontrolled hypertension, obesity, HIV infection, and untreated sleep apnea. Multiple comorbidities remain undertreated, and key laboratory data are missing, indicating significant gaps in chronic disease management and follow‑up.
